done_when: The synced Forge skill tells the agent, the first time each of these happens for a person, to add one plain sentence saying what just happened and what they can do next: a story plan shown for approval, a cold read finding, a part starting, a pull request ready, a merge, a prototype demo, sign-off; never repeating it, never naming commands unless asked; a test checks each moment through forge sync and forge init

dismissals.because: tests/test_fix_people_using_forge_through_the_agent_don.py:35 whether a sentence teaches the right next step is a judgement about wording, which this review makes, not something a test can check; the test proves each moment ships with a one-sentence example holding both parts through forge sync and forge init, and tests/test_split_ships.py pins the synced skill to its reviewed source

findings.body: The new assertions check sentence shape and word counts, but not whether the next step relates to the moment. Replacing every delivered example with "A thing has happened today; you can eat lunch now." would pass through both forge sync and forge init, even though none of the seven moments teaches the person what to do next. This is new evidence beyond the previous review's "OK." example, which the added assertions now reject. Assert a meaningful next action for each delivered moment.
findings.title: Not done: the sync/init test verifies each coaching sentence's event-specific next step

why: People using Forge through the agent don't learn how Forge works, because the agent does each step without telling them what just happened or what they can do next
